eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study analyzes adult heart transplant recipients using non-linear machine learning models (e.g., random forests, XGBoost) to predict survival outcomes, includes relevant clinical comparators, and is a peer‑reviewed article published in 2020.

identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective analysis of UNOS heart transplant data using a two-stage machine learning framework with isotonic regression calibration.
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included all heart transplant events in the UNOS dataset up to September 30, 2016.
identification_methods.Design: Two-stage machine learning framework: independent models per time period followed by isotonic regression calibration.
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: Logistic Regression, Linear Discriminant Analysis, Artificial Neural Networks, CART, SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost; final model logistic regression with LASSO feature selection.
identification_methods.Class Imbalance: Addressed using sub‑sampling methods: up‑sampling, down‑sampling, SMOTE, and ROSE.
identification_methods.Comparator: Standard machine learning models without isotonic regression calibration.
identification_methods.Input Variables: Pre‑operative donor and recipient variables (originally 494, reduced after cleaning and feature engineering).
identification_methods.Missing Data Handling: Removed variables with >90% missing; numeric median imputation, categorical unknown imputation for remaining missing values.
identification_methods.Validation Method: 5‑fold cross‑validation on training set and 20% hold‑out test set.
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Used 5‑fold CV for model selection, isotonic regression to enforce monotonicity, code and analysis publicly available on GitHub.

population.Population Notes: National UNOS dataset of U.S. heart transplants from 1987 to 2016

interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: Pre-operative tabular clinical variables from UNOS registry
interventions_outcomes.Temporal Handling: Multi-period static baseline predictions for 1 month to 10 years post‑transplant
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Two-stage framework: Stage I independent ML models per time‑point, Stage II isotonic regression to enforce monotonic decreasing survival probabilities
interventions_outcomes.Reported outcomes in study: AUC, G‑Mean, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity for survival prediction at 1 month–10 years
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Primary focus on discrimination (AUC) and calibration; isotonic regression improves metrics
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: Isotonic regression generally increased AUC and G‑Mean across time points
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome group: All heart transplant recipients in the hold‑out test set
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reporting: AUC 0.581 (pre‑calibration), improved to 0.598 after isotonic regression
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: Area under the ROC curve on a held‑out test cohort
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: AUC comparable to literature; isotonic regression yields modest improvement
